# A function reading only its parameter, named like a var of the page, called
# from a component android composes on its own (the provider hands chip a
# value of the context). Android matched state by name, took `name` for the
# page's var, and made shout a member of the state class, which chip called
# through a `state` it does not have.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// Reads only its parameter, which is named like the page's var.
func shout(name string) string {
    var out list[string] = []
    for var part = string.split(name, "-") {
        out.push(string.upper(part))
    }
    return out.join(" ")
}

// What a chip says after its label.
context #suffix("!")

// Composed on its own on android, since the provider around it hands it a
// value of the context.
component chip(label string, @tap()) ui.node {
    ui.button(text=shout(label) + suffix, @click { tap() })
}

component page ui.node {
    var name = "a-page"
    var picked = ""

    ui.vbox {
        ui.text #title(value=shout(name))
        suffix("?") {
            for var item = ["b", "c"] {
                chip #chips(label=item, @tap { picked = item })
            }
        }
    }
}

func testChipCallsAPureFunc(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.title.value == "A PAGE")
    c.chips[1].tap()
    t.assert(c.picked == "c")
}
